page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-96 is an instance configuration within the Network Optimized C4 series, engineered for high-concurrency enterprise workloads. It operates on the x86_64 CPU architecture, providing 96 dedicated virtual cores and 360.0 GB of system memory. This configuration offers a ratio of 3.75 GB of RAM per core, delivering a balanced capacity for multi-threaded computation without over-allocating physical memory resources.

The instance contains no integrated GPU accelerators and does not include local disk storage. Consequently, all persistent data and operating system installations require external network-attached volumes. In addition, the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating network configuration through private addresses, cloud NAT, or separately provisioned public IPs.

Regarding cost efficiency, the c4n-standard-96 consolidates substantial compute capacity into a single instance footprint, which reduces multi-node management overhead for large processing tasks. The primary technical tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O performance relies entirely on network attached storage throughput. Best-fit workloads include distributed database instances, large-scale CI/CD build pipelines, network functions virtualization, ETL processing, and high-throughput web serving architectures.
